# vendor

Pdfium, downloaded here. Nothing in this folder is in git — this note is the exception, and the only
thing that is (see the end of `.gitignore`).

The app **loads** Pdfium at run time rather than linking against it (see `src/pdfium/`), which is why
the library has to be *somewhere* rather than being built into the executable:

```text
vendor/
    lib/                    the library the app loads, and the one a build copies next to the exe
                              libpdfium.dylib (macOS) or pdfium.dll (Windows)
    include/*.h             the C headers that library was built with — the ABI this app declares
    VERSION                 which Pdfium build it is
    args.gn                 the GN arguments that build was made with
    LICENSE, licenses/      Pdfium's own licences, carried with it
```

## The build in this folder

**PDFium 160.0.8179.0** — `pdfium-binaries` release `chromium/8179`, published 2026-11-23 and
downloaded 2026-11-27.

| | macOS arm64 (what this tree holds) | Windows x64 |
|---|---|---|
| Archive | `pdfium-mac-arm64.tgz` | `pdfium-win-x64.tgz` |
| Release | <https://github.com/bblanchon/pdfium-binaries/releases/tag/chromium%2F8179> | same release |
| Archive SHA-256 | `44b7c6f55dd33454d0909728bd0adf6c86a8e141b36f07a6b6f50e228e1dfb46` | `836a77c9053f624839c66010cddea7b675628a36b8831d2330178bb169d241b6` |
| Library SHA-256 | `fa68216ccec6dbdd3b9f46d7a8c921ebfdf942dd542c8f816738b87fcd0018b8` (`lib/libpdfium.dylib`) | `b9324fe77556753e24443b8ff1d03b39a3aa01ccd6e56e7debb82922438e8965` (`lib/pdfium.dll`) |
| Built with | arm64, release, **no V8, no XFA** (`args.gn`) | x64, release, **no V8, no XFA** |

Both come from the same release, so one `include/`, `VERSION` and `args.gn` describe either: the
public headers are byte-identical between the two archives. A tree is set up for the platform it is
built on, and moving to the other means replacing the library **and** the headers as a pair.

The import library in the Windows release (`lib/pdfium.dll.lib`) is deliberately not copied: the app
resolves its entry points with `GetProcAddress` and never links against Pdfium.

## Where it comes from

A **`pdfium-binaries`** release: prebuilt Pdfium, from
<https://github.com/bblanchon/pdfium-binaries/releases> — `pdfium-mac-arm64.tgz` or
`pdfium-win-x64.tgz`. Its own layout is this one: unpack `lib/libpdfium.dylib` (or `bin/pdfium.dll`)
into `vendor/lib/`, and `include/`, `VERSION`, `args.gn` and the licences beside it.

The stability promise this wrapper relies on is Pdfium's own: the files in its `public/` directory
are the API for embedders, and code outside it may change at any time
(<https://pdfium.googlesource.com/pdfium/+/refs/heads/main/README.md>). That is why
`src/pdfium/api.rs` names only public entry points, and only the ones the app calls.

**The headers matter as much as the library.** `FPDF_GetPageSizeByIndexF` takes an `FS_SIZEF*`; the
older `FPDF_GetPageSizeByIndex` beside it takes two `double*`s. `src/pdfium/api.rs` declares what
`vendor/include` says — a library from a build whose header differs may load and then write the wrong
size through the wrong pointer. That is why the headers are vendored with the library rather than
generated by a binding for "some" Pdfium version.

## Updating it

1. Pick the newest `chromium/<build>` release on the `pdfium-binaries` releases page and read its
   `VERSION` and `args.gn`. Take the archive for the platform being built on —
   `pdfium-mac-arm64.tgz` or `pdfium-win-x64.tgz`.
2. Download it, verify the SHA-256 GitHub publishes for the asset — the API's asset `digest` field
   carries it — and unpack it.
3. Copy it over this folder. macOS and Linux:
   ```sh
   new=/path/to/extracted/pdfium
   cp "$new/lib/libpdfium.dylib" vendor/lib/libpdfium.dylib
   cp "$new"/include/*.h vendor/include/
   cp -R "$new"/licenses/. vendor/licenses/
   cp "$new/LICENSE" "$new/VERSION" "$new/args.gn" vendor/
   ```
   Windows:
   ```powershell
   $new = 'C:\path\to\extracted\pdfium'
   Copy-Item "$new\bin\pdfium.dll" vendor\lib\pdfium.dll -Force
   Copy-Item "$new\include\*" vendor\include -Recurse -Force
   Copy-Item "$new\licenses\*" vendor\licenses -Force
   Copy-Item "$new\LICENSE", "$new\VERSION", "$new\args.gn" vendor -Force
   ```
4. Run `cargo test`. The wrapper resolves thirty-two symbols and checks the C layouts it uses, and
   `pdf::tests` and `pdfium::render::tests` render real fixtures: a public-header change shows up
   there rather than in a release build. Diff `vendor/include` against the previous headers before
   accepting the update — the declarations in `src/pdfium/api.rs` follow those files, not a binding
   for another version. `fpdfview.h` was unchanged from 8125 to 8179, which is the expected shape of
   an update within one major version.

`build.rs` watches `vendor/VERSION` and `vendor/lib`, so an update is noticed by the next build.

## What a build does with it

`build.rs` copies `vendor/lib/*.dll` next to the executable a build produces, so
`target/release/cheap-note.exe` and `pdfium.dll` are a pair that can be started from anywhere or copied
to another machine. A build with no `vendor/lib` says so as a warning, and the app it produces runs
without PDF support — a state the app is designed for: it starts, draws, writes ink, and refuses to
open a PDF with a message rather than a crash.
